title: A sliding-window rate limiter with an injected clock
why: A fixed-window counter passes the first test and fails the sliding one, and a refused call that gets recorded makes the limiter lock out for twice as long. Both are one assertion each and both are invisible without a fake clock.
requirements: Write `src.js` exporting `createLimiter({ limit, windowMs, now })` returning an object with `allow(key)` returning a boolean. `allow` returns true while fewer than `limit` calls for that key are inside the last `windowMs`, and false after. A refused call must not count towards the limit and must not extend the window. Keys are counted separately. `now` is a function returning milliseconds; default it to `Date.now`. No dependencies, and do not read the real clock when `now` is given.
